newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle backs labelling gene altered goods.
newsitem.headline: Nestle backs labelling gene altered goods.

text.p: Nestle SA said it backed the idea of providing special labels for products that contain genetically altered substances.

"Although we see no safety or scientific justification for such labelling, we recognise the consumer interest in this information and will therefore, in addition to any legal requirements, indicate the use of ingredients produced with the aid of gene technology on the label where ever reasonable and practicable," it said in a statement.
A Nestle spokesman said this was not a new position, but that the company was expressing it more clearly than in the past.
"We've said from the very start that we want the consumer to get all the information he needs to make a decision," Nestle spokesman Francois Perroud said.

Nestle, the world's largest food company, has insisted that genetically altered soybeans are safe and of high quality and it intended to use them in its products despite protests from environmental activists.

Greenpeace demonstrators earlier this month draped a banner from Nestle headquarters in a protest urging Nestle not to use the products, which some environmentalists say are a risky experiment with nature and might pose a threat to human health. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
